question: Can a neural network decide during training when, where, and how to add width or depth, while preserving its current function and targeting capacity that improves natural-gradient progress?

key_findings.claim: SENN scores a proposed expansion by how much it enlarges the output-gradient component expressible by the model's local parameter tangent space.
key_findings.evidence: The natural expansion score is eta=g-transpose F-inverse g, interpreted as the dataset-normalized squared projection of the output gradient onto the Jacobian image. A proposal is accepted when its relative score increase exceeds tau and its absolute increase exceeds alpha, unifying when, where, and initialization choice under one criterion.

anchors.section: Expansion score and four SENN ingredients

key_findings.claim: Width and depth can be inserted without an immediate change to the represented function, reducing catastrophic optimization disruption.
key_findings.evidence: Width concatenates new features while initializing their outgoing weights to zero. MLP depth insertion composes an invertible transform, identity-capable rational activation, and inverse transform; DenseNet-style skip connections make layer insertion easier by routing the old function around a zero-output new branch.

key_findings.claim: The paper proves bounded successive additions and derives a tractable conservative score under a Kronecker-factored curvature approximation.
key_findings.evidence: Because eta is bounded by the full output-gradient norm, repeated relative improvements yield fewer than 1+(log lambda-log alpha)/log(1+tau) immediate additions. With layerwise KFAC, a residual-gradient expression provides a lower bound on the true expansion-score increase and accounts for activation redundancy that diagonal gradient scores miss.

key_findings.claim: Toy and image experiments show plausible capacity placement, stable anytime behavior, and adaptation of model size to data complexity.
key_findings.evidence: A regression example adds localized basis functions where residual error remains; half-moons training inserts two hidden layers as the boundary needs more expressivity. Across five MNIST seeds, a 10-unit start grows to roughly 50-60 hidden units and exceeds 97% validation accuracy; DenseNet-style CIFAR-10 training reports over 93% while growing and pruning without validation drops.

key_findings.claim: Transfer expansion provides a modest gain, but the study does not establish compute-efficient superiority over competing growth or search methods.
key_findings.evidence: Expanding a CIFAR-10-pretrained DenseNet during Tiny ImageNet transfer improves test accuracy by a reported relative 3-4% over standard transfer from 48.2%. Yet experiments lack matched wall-clock/FLOP comparisons to GradMax, Firefly, Net2Net, or fixed-size training, while the implementation considers many proposals using optimization and KFAC state.

method.core_idea: Grow only those function-preserving neurons or layers that expand the locally useful natural-gradient subspace by a sufficient amount.
method.mechanism: SENN generates candidate width/depth additions, initializes them so the network output is unchanged, estimates proposal utility with a KFAC-based lower bound to the natural expansion-score increase, optimizes or samples candidate initializations, accepts the best above relative and absolute thresholds, and can reverse the calculation to prune features.
assumptions: Local quadratic loss and Fisher/KFAC curvature approximate the value of added capacity.
Function-preserving insertion is possible for the architecture and activation family.
Finite candidate proposals include a useful location and initialization.
Hand-set relative, absolute, and layer-scaling thresholds transfer across training regimes.

techniques.role: Measures additional locally expressible loss-reducing direction after a candidate architecture change.
Adds width or depth without erasing the current learned mapping.
Accounts for redundancy and makes candidate scoring more tractable than full Fisher inversion.
Uses related curvature information to remove capacity and later regrow it if training demands.

evaluations.setting: One-dimensional regression and half-moons binary classification
evaluations.metric: proposal-score landscapes, function error, selected neuron positions, depth, and decision boundaries
evaluations.result: Proposals concentrate on residual-error regions and layer insertions occur when shallower boundaries saturate.
evaluations.baseline: Earlier training phases and rejected proposal locations; no competing growth method.

evaluations.setting: MNIST subsets and full MNIST, five seeds
evaluations.metric: validation accuracy, total hidden units, and growth trajectory
evaluations.result: A small start grows reproducibly to about 50-60 hidden units and exceeds 97%; final size responds nonlinearly to dataset subset size.
evaluations.baseline: Different dataset fractions and the initial 10-unit architecture.

evaluations.metric: accuracy, architecture trajectories, grow-prune stability, and relative transfer gain
evaluations.result: CIFAR-10 stays around 90-93% under cyclic perturbations; adaptive transfer reports a 3-4% relative test-accuracy gain over 48.2% standard transfer.
evaluations.baseline: Standard transfer learning and internal architecture trajectories, not matched competing growth algorithms.

limitations: The score inherits local-quadratic, Fisher-equals-useful-curvature, and KFAC factorization errors.
Image experiments lack matched compute, memory, and accuracy comparisons against the strongest dynamic-growth and fixed-architecture baselines.
Proposal search can be expensive: reported settings optimize thousands of neuron proposals and many layer proposals and maintain curvature statistics.
Thresholds, separate layer-score scaling factors, proposal frequency, damping, and pruning rules are manually tuned.
MLP depth preservation requires invertible maps and identity-capable activations; other architectures need bespoke morphisms.
Evaluation stops at modest vision models and does not demonstrate the claimed transformer or continual-learning extensions.
failure_modes: Curvature approximation overvalues redundant proposals or systematically favors early layers.
Zero outgoing initialization blocks or delays useful gradient flow into a newly added feature.
Expansion threshold oscillates with optimizer or learning-rate changes, causing growth-prune churn.
Proposal search misses a coordinated multi-layer change whose individual additions appear unhelpful.
Dynamic recompilation and quadratic KFAC state erase any training savings from starting small.
reusable_insights: Architecture growth should be scored on new functional directions after conditioning on existing directions, not raw new-parameter gradients.
A function-preserving morphism enables clean before/after causal tests of added capacity.
Dynamic architecture papers should include total proposal-search and recompilation cost, not only final parameter count and accuracy.
Growth and pruning are best treated as reversible decisions under one criterion when training conditions change.
open_questions: Can low-rank or sketch-based curvature make the score competitive at transformer scale?
How well does score-predicted improvement correlate with realized held-out improvement after controlling for compute?
Can thresholds be derived from uncertainty, resource budgets, or sequential hypothesis tests instead of tuned constants?
Does dynamic growth beat compute-matched dense, sparse, and progressive-scaling baselines on modern language and vision training?

competitive_landscape.title: Net2Net: Accelerating Learning via Knowledge Transfer
competitive_landscape.difference: Net2WiderNet and Net2DeeperNet establish function-preserving width/depth transformations for manually chosen expansions. SENN adds a natural-gradient criterion for when, where, and how to expand, at the price of costly curvature and proposal machinery.

competitive_landscape.title: Splitting Steepest Descent for Growing Neural Architectures
competitive_landscape.difference: Splitting Steepest Descent grows width by second-order functional neuron splitting near convergence. SENN can introduce both novel width and depth earlier and explicitly conditions on natural-gradient redundancy, but has weaker matched benchmark evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Firefly Neural Architecture Descent: a General Approach for Growing Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Firefly searches a functional neighborhood and greedily grows width or depth, with neural-architecture-search and continual-learning benchmarks. SENN's natural-gradient score offers a cohesive redundancy-aware rationale and reversible pruning, but does not compare against Firefly empirically.

competitive_landscape.title: GradMax: Growing Neural Networks using Gradient Information
competitive_landscape.difference: GradMax uses SVD to initialize added neurons for maximum new-weight gradient and demonstrates broad vision results. SENN argues raw gradients ignore redundancy and uses KFAC natural-gradient gain while also adding depth; a direct cost-quality comparison is missing.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Grow Pretrained Models for Efficient Transformer Training
competitive_landscape.difference: LiGO learns structured width/depth mappings from a smaller pretrained transformer and reports up to 50% training-compute savings. SENN discovers capacity online from optimization geometry and need not target a predetermined size, but its transformer scalability and net savings are only proposed future work.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after primary-source comparison: the novel center is a redundancy-aware natural-gradient expansion score that jointly answers when, where, and initialization for both width and depth, with a reversible pruning interpretation. Function-preserving growth and gradient-based growth are well established; without direct compute-matched competitor results or transformer-scale validation, SENN remains a sophisticated and promising criterion rather than a demonstrated best growth system.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed all 17 extracted pages, including theorem proofs, curvature appendices, proposal-search details, implementation workarounds, every experiment, and cited growth methods. Five primary competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
